title: Allocentric Embedding Credit Fabrication & Rerank Commitment Model
creator: Sana Patel
description:
Objective: Design and validate a hybrid per-vector + batch-slot pricing model that (1) preserves unit economics for small/medium customers, (2) offers clear cost savings for high-volume rerank workloads, and (3) maps cleanly onto enterprise QSA/compliance flows.

Scope: Experimentation plan covering: a) per-vector baseline price and time-decayed microcredits, b) batch-slot bundles with burst credits for rerank pipelines, c) commit tiers for enterprise contracts with automated slot allocation, and d) billing semantics (rounding, proration, refunds).

Success criteria: (1) Reduce average $/rerank request by 20% for top-10% traffic customers while maintaining >=95% revenue capture vs projected baseline; (2) No >3% churn in customers on trial during pilot; (3) Enterprise QSA sign-off on billing language + security disclosures.

Deliverables:
- Pricing simulation spreadsheet (link below) with traffic segments and revenue sensitivity
- Prototype billing engine rules for batch-slot allocation (GH PR link)
- Confluence PRD describing contract language and QSA artifacts
- Pilot cohort enrollment plan (10 customers across churn-risk and high-volume use cases)

Experiment design notes:
- We define a microcredit: 1 microcredit = 1 vector-equivalent at baseline precision. Microcredits decay over a 30-day window to encourage steady usage and limit arbitrage.
- Batch-slot: a time-limited reservation that converts to per-vector consumption when used; unused slots roll into burst credits with a 14-day expiry. This is to support rerank bursts without long-term revenue erosion.
- Commit tiers: 3 tiers (Bronze/Silver/Gold) with discounted per-vector rates + guaranteed baseline slots and priority capacity. Contract language must include overage rates and audit rights.

- Simulation sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1_simulate_PRICE
- PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Allocentric+Embed+Credits+PRD

Open questions:
1) How to present microcredit decay in invoices concisely? Proposal: show 'microcredit usage' line item and 'decay adjustment' only when decay >5% in billing period.
2) Taxonomy alignment with existing per-vector meters (embeddings vs. rerank embeddings). Need ENG to confirm meters.
3) Legal/QSA review scope: Is burst-credit expiry considered a 'financial instrument' in certain markets? Run by Legal.

- Week 2: ship billing prototype + internal demo (owner: Eng-Billing)
- Week 3: contract language draft for QSA + Security (owner: Sana)
- Week 4: begin pilot outreach, sign 5 initial customers (owner: Solutions)
